Changelog

Mirrored from cli/mix-shell/CHANGELOG.md, where releases update it. The component's page is mix-shell. This page describes the current main branch of MixOS.

Unreleased

Changed

  • mix man reads the manual built into the binary: every docs/mix/*.md page is packed into one zstd frame at build time, so a binary copied alone, with no checkout and no network, has its whole manual. With no MIXOS_MAN_* variable set the built-in page wins (it documents exactly this binary), then files on disk, then the online copy. MIXOS_MAN_SOURCE=local puts files on disk first, then the built-in manual, and never uses the network. MIXOS_MAN_SOURCE=auto or MIXOS_MAN_URL keeps the online-first order, with the built-in manual before a stale cached copy. mix doctor and mix apropos count and search the built-in pages. The compiled-in path to the build checkout's docs/mix is no longer a lookup candidate.

Fixed

  • A foreground job stopped (^Z) just after its exec is now stopped, not reported as "job stopped before exec acknowledgement" and aborted. The launch checked for the stop before reading the exec acknowledgement that was already waiting. This was the intermittent failure of the owned_editor_pty test foreground_job_ctrl_z_fg_and_nested_editor_stop_preserve_draft.

0.116.0

Added

  • Released with mix 0.116.0: the remote mix binary for ssh_mix and the other remote-mix builtins comes from the mix_bin option, else MIX_REMOTE_BIN, else the old install path's mix (mix man remote).

0.115.0

Added

  • Released with mix 0.115.0: unix_connect() opens a local unix-domain stream socket, with NUL-terminated frames for Varlink and hostd (mix man system).

0.114.0

Changed

  • Usage statistics are an append-only JSONL store. A run's exit appends one record to runs/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl with a single write and does nothing else, so recording costs nothing measurable: mix -c 1 went from 151 ms to 52 ms on a host with a busy history, the same as with stats off. Raw day files are never rewritten; cache/ holds disposable per-day aggregates checked against the exact raw file; reports filter by each bucket's own date. mix stats query runs SQL over the old mix.db tables built in memory, so on a large history it now takes about a second.
  • clear and reset append an operation anchored to storage positions, not a clock, under ops.lock. They refuse while the old weekly documents (current.json, YYYY-WNN.json) exist; those are read in place, never moved, and their stats.lock is never taken, so an older mix still writing them keeps working. mix man stats documents the store.

Fixed

  • A session task no longer inherits file descriptors the shell itself inherited without close-on-exec.

0.113.1

Fixed

  • Built on mix 0.113.1: on dopus-test.command.executed (a hyphenated handler name) now fires; before, it parsed and never did. mix man bus documents it.

0.113.0

Added

  • Built on mix 0.113.0 with the mime feature: mime_type() names a file's type as the desktop does. mix man io documents it.

0.112.1

Fixed

  • Built on mix 0.112.1: SIGTERM and Ctrl-C end a blocking tcp_accept, tcp_recv, tcp_recv_line or ws_recv at once, tcp_send takes a whole-send {timeout} (TCP_SEND_TIMEOUT), and receives serve buffered data first while traffic that delivers nothing counts against the deadline. mix man system documents them.

0.112.0

Added

  • Built on mix 0.112.0: server-side TCP (tcp_listen, tcp_accept, tcp_local_addr, tcp_on on a listener) and on @.verb, which registers a handler under the --serve name so one generic script serves any instance. mix man serve and mix man system document both.

Fixed

  • The serve reload lifecycle test's TERM-ignoring fixture creates the trace file itself. The citizen spawned it before the first trace line existed, so a fast start panicked on open and the grace test timed out.

0.111.0

Fixed

  • An interrupted run exits with status 130 (128+SIGINT) derived from the signal actually received, never from error text: an ordinary error whose message mentions interrupted now fails with its own diagnostic instead of exiting 0.
  • SIGINT/SIGTERM are honoured during --serve startup (stalled broker registration, CPU-bound preludes, reloads) and during -c, script and .mixrc prelude loading. A caught interrupt cannot end in success, and --result-fd always reports it as an error frame.
  • script_path() is resolved before the prelude runs in script and serve modes.

0.109.4

Initial MixOS shell transplant. Language semantics retain the source version. Application transport is native ABP through noded. Runtime directories use the shared config rule; installed manuals are available offline. Cross-process native-session handoff bytes retain the frozen compatibility contract.
